text:
Priya Patel: hi team - I changed my address to OR last week but this paycheck shows NY state tax withheld as well as OR. did my location switch not propagate?

Sam (People Ops): thanks for flagging. can you share the stub lines (redact amounts) and the date you updated your profile?

Priya Patel: updated profile on 04/05 via self-service. paystub: 
```
Pay period: 04/01 - 04/15
Gross: $7,200.00
Federal Tax: $1,100.00
State Tax - NY: $360.00
State Tax - OR: $216.00
Net: $5,524.00
```
I moved to OR on 04/03 and updated address on 04/05. expected only OR withholding for this run.

Payroll Bot: Auto: payrun pr-98011 completed. HRIS import snapshot for RED-5587 shows residence_state change event timestamp 1965426000. However payroll jurisdiction mapping for state withholding pulled employee payroll_state=NY from legacy_location table because payrun snapshot used location snapshot at 1965412000. A sync race condition detected.

Diego - Payroll: yep looks like a timing race. HRIS change landed after payroll snapshot window. Our payroll snapshot cutoff was 1965415000. Because the residence change was after cutoff but before pay period end, system treated employee as NY for withholding which created an extra state tax. We need to reverse the NY withholding and re-run tax calc for OR-only.

Lena (Finance): if we reverse NY withholding we need to confirm tax deposit timing. When was the transmit step for pr-98011?

Payroll Bot: transmit step timestamp: 1965430500 (tax remittance transmitted to state vendors).

Diego - Payroll: transmit already occurred. remediation path: 1) issue off-cycle correction to reverse NY withholding and adjust net pay; 2) coordinate with Finance to reclaim NY deposit or record as variance and file amendment. For the employee, we'll do an off-cycle reversal to correct net. Also we'll update the HRIS->payroll snapshot logic to prefer residence_state change events tagged as "move" within 7 days of pay period to be applied retroactively when possible.

Sam (People Ops): Priya - we'll correct this ASAP. Diego: can you draft the reversal and aim for off-cycle tomorrow? Lena: can you own deposit follow-up?

Diego - Payroll: drafting off-cycle stub: 
```
Reversal: StateTax_NY_Reversal -$360.00
Tax recalc: OR state tax remains $216.00
Net delta to employee: +$360.00
Notes: reversal for duplicate state withholding due to HRIS->payroll snapshot race. Audit ref pr-98011 -> pr-98011-rev.
```
Scheduling off-cycle for 1965432800.

Lena (Finance): will contact state vendor about reclaim. If vendor allows reclaim, we will reverse deposit; if not, will record variance and adjust at monthly reconciliation. I'll post follow-up by EOD.

Payroll Bot: off-cycle job queued pr-98011-rev at 1965432800.

Priya Patel: thank you. will this affect my state tax filings? do I need to file anything in NY to claim refund?

Lena (Finance): usually the employer-side correction will fix withholding amounts reported on your W-2. If a withholding deposit remains with NY state and isn't reclaimed, you as an individual can claim a refund on your NY return for amounts incorrectly withheld after we provide an employer letter. We'll aim to handle it on employer side first.

Diego - Payroll: off-cycle processed at 1965433000. Reversal posted and corrected stub generated. Payroll Bot: pr-98011-rev: SUCCESS.

Payroll Bot: Notification: bank ACH for adjustment initiated; employee should see corrected net adjustment pending settlement.

Priya Patel: saw the pending in my bank portal, thanks everyone. appreciate quick response.

Sam (People Ops): we'll add a fix to snapshot cutoff logic and raise a ticket to ensure ResidenceChange events within 7 days of payrun are re-evaluated. Also adding a test to simulate post-cutoff moves.

Lena (Finance): update - vendor response: NY vendor accepts reclaim request; processing time 5-10 business days. Filing ticket FIN-2026-77 to track.

Priya Patel: thanks all :thumbsup:
